causes_to_rate.c: AliExpress catalog feel — reads as a marketplace thumbnail, not organic TikTok
causes_to_rate.d: Generic hook text — no specific number/problem/surprise

a.evidence: 0/0.5/1/1.5/2/2.5s frames are pixel-identical -- the same static glossy car-organizer product photo used across all 4 variants, with zero motion for the full 3-second hook. The scene only changes at 3s, cutting to a gray AliExpress price screenshot.

b.evidence: The product is clearly visible and identifiable at 0s -- same fully-in-frame organizer/tray shot as the other variants.

c.evidence: Same staged AliExpress-style hero photo as the other 3 variants: stock tablet video, branded bottles, snack box with visible Chinese text, composited sunset backdrop. Marketplace-listing look, not organic footage.

d.evidence: Hook text 'הגב של המושב ברכב שלי היה בלאגן מוחלט' ('my car seat back was a total mess') names a specific personal problem (unlike 007B's fully generic curiosity line), but 'בלאגן מוחלט' ('total mess') itself is a vague, unspecific descriptor -- no concrete detail of what the mess was (spills, kids' stuff, wrappers, etc.), so it's a real problem statement without a sharp specific hook.

e.evidence: Hook text promises a 'before' scene of chaos/mess ('בלאגן מוחלט'), but the opening frame at 0s already shows the pristine, fully-organized solved state -- bottles neatly seated, tablet propped up, snacks arranged on the tray. There is no messy 'before' shown at all during the entire static 3-second hook; the text's problem claim is never visually paid off in the opening.

h.evidence: 'הגב של המושב ברכב שלי היה בלאגן מוחלט' is natural, personal, first-person Hebrew ('ברכב שלי' = 'in my car') with an idiomatic phrase ('בלאגן מוחלט') that a native speaker would plausibly say -- reads as organic, not translated.
